# Baseball Theater v3 — Checkable backlog

**Purpose:** Turn [FEATURES](./FEATURES.md) + [ARCHITECTURE](./ARCHITECTURE.md) + [VISUAL-DESIGN](./VISUAL-DESIGN.md) into increments a loop can finish without a human “looks good” step.

**Where to edit:** this file is **generated**. Each story lives in `docs/v3/backlog/stories/S<N>.md` (open `docs/v3/backlog/` as an Obsidian vault, or edit the files directly); everything around the stories — these rules, the reviews, the baseline, the gap map — lives in `docs/v3/backlog/frame/`. In a story note, edit `title`, `table_title`, `priority`, and `status` in the frontmatter and everything else in the body; the other frontmatter fields are derived. Then run `pnpm backlog:build`, which rewrites this file (the heading, `**Status:**` line, and status table included) and normalizes the notes. `pnpm backlog:check` (part of `pnpm verify` and CI) fails when they are out of sync, and the pre-commit hook rebuilds on commit and refuses hand edits to this file. Details: [VAULT-MIGRATION](./VAULT-MIGRATION.md) V3.

**Rules for every story**

1. Acceptance criteria map to **commands, tests, or file invariants** (exit codes / assertions).
2. Vague phrases (“works correctly”, “handles errors gracefully”) are **forbidden** until rewritten.
3. Done means **`scripts/verify-<ID>.sh` exits 0** *and* **`pnpm verify` exits 0** *and* Status is `done` in the story's note (`docs/v3/backlog/stories/<ID>.md`, rebuilt into this file by `pnpm backlog:build` before the grader runs) *and* the run is captured in [AUDIT](./AUDIT.md) via `scripts/audit.sh story <ID>`, committed with the code. An uncaptured green run leaves no evidence it happened.
4. Prefer the smallest story that moves the carried product loop forward. When UI and data-model work compete, **prefer MLB API + ingest/projection stories** — UI should follow how BT stores and organizes data. **Exceptions:** **S24** (brand theme), **S26** (typed API route contract), **S27** (spec + breaking-change gate), **S25** (typed client query cache), and **S29** (spec-fidelity gate — re-scoped 2026-09-16; the `openapi-fetch` DAL adoption is a Later theme; owner 2026-10-14: our own client adopts it, no trigger) run before UI fill stories **S2–S5**, and the design stories **S31–S34** (rule 18) run before the UI stories they gate, so new UI does not copy the night-park/teal scaffold ([VISUAL-DESIGN](./VISUAL-DESIGN.md)) or the ad-hoc `useEffect` + `fetch` pattern, and so every route added later is gated from birth ([ADR-014](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-014--client-state-management-accepted) / [ADR-015](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-015--api-versioning--compatibility-accepted) / [ADR-016](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-016--generated-client-dal-from-the-openapi-spec-accepted)). **S25 runs before S29** (re-ordered 2026-09-13 review): S25 unblocks eight downstream stories and S29 unblocks none, so the codegen fidelity loop does not gate the carried loop — see [Backlog reviews](#backlog-reviews).
5. When starting a story, set `status: doing` in its note (`docs/v3/backlog/stories/<ID>.md`) and run `pnpm backlog:build`. When all acceptance criteria pass, set `status: done` and run `pnpm backlog:build` **before** the grader (graders read `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`), in the same change set as the implementation (do not leave status stale). The **Story status** table, and its order, are generated from each note's `status` and `priority` — never edit or re-sort them by hand; to re-prioritize, change `priority` in the notes.
6. **Do not start the next story/goal** until the finished story is **committed** (clean `git status` for that work, or an explicit commit SHA on the branch). Uncommitted “done” work blocks the next goal — reject moving on and commit (or ask the user to) first.
7. **First work item is always the grader.** Sub-item 0 writes `scripts/verify-<ID>.sh`. After that file exists, the rest of the story must not modify `scripts/` or `test/` (see Goal condition). Colocated `*.test.ts(x)` next to source are allowed when their directory is in `<paths>`.
8. Each story has a copy-paste **`/goal` command**. It points at `scripts/verify-<ID>.sh` instead of restating checks. Creating that one file (Work item 0) is the only allowed `scripts/` change; after it exists, do not edit `scripts/` or `test/`.
9. **Prove the grader red before green.** A run must execute the new `scripts/verify-<ID>.sh` against current HEAD and surface the nonzero exit *before* any product code is written. A grader first seen passing proves nothing: a weak script plus a weak implementation goes green and you learn nothing. (Only **S1** is exempt — it is already implemented, so its script must pass on HEAD.)
10. **The scope fence is hard.** If an acceptance criterion cannot be met inside a story’s **Scope files**, the run **stops and reports** the criterion and the path it needs. Widening the fence mid-run is never the agent’s call — the story was mis-scoped, so fix the story.
11. **Do not start a story while a backlog review is due.** Check [AUDIT](./AUDIT.md) and the [Backlog reviews](#backlog-reviews) scheduling notes first: due after **6** `done` stories since the last row, or immediately on a drift event (story count doubled from 3 by the owner, 2026-10-21). This is a sequencing gate like rule 6 — a due review blocks the next story the same way uncommitted work does.
12. **Every story ships a numeric turn cap.** `N` is not a cap. If a defensible number can’t be named, the story isn't bounded yet — fix the ambiguity (pick the tree, fix the document set, cut the scope) until it can be. Record the assumption the cap rests on next to it. **A turn is one agent turn of the `/goal` loop** (the agent works, then stops and the goal is re-checked), **not a tool call** (2026-10-24 backlog review, from practice: S76 finished in one turn with about 30 tool calls against a cap of 14, and every earlier story's diff is far larger than its cap in tool calls; confirmed by the owner 2026-10-25: *"Whatever is most typical"*). A design story's cap counts those turns across all its sessions.

13. **`docs/v3/AUDIT.md` and the backlog notes are always inside every story's fence.** The ledger entry
    ships in the same commit as the code (rule 3), so every story's **Scope files** and `/goal` path list
    include `docs/v3/AUDIT.md` — added to all `todo` stories on 2026-09-09. Written only by
    `scripts/audit.sh`, never by hand. Likewise the story's status flip (rule 5) touches its note under
    `docs/v3/backlog/` and the generated `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md` (via `pnpm backlog:build`), so both belong
    in every fence — the whole directory, because rule 17's baseline and these review notes live in
    `docs/v3/backlog/frame/`, not in the story's own note. Added to all `todo` stories by the 2026-09-13
    backlog review that followed vault-migration V3.

14. **If an acceptance criterion forces a new runtime dependency, the dependency manifests are in the fence.**
    Any story whose ACs require adding a package (a real SDK, a generator, a client lib) must list the
    manifest files that `pnpm install` will touch — the workspace `package.json` **and** root
    `pnpm-lock.yaml` — in its **Scope files**, Goal condition and `/goal` command. Three reviews running
    caught the same trap: S14 and S15 needed the root `package.json` for a new script; S7 needs
    `functions/package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` for the Firestore SDK. Deriving the fence from the ACs at
    authoring time is the fix; this rule is the backstop. A story that hits an un-fenced manifest mid-run
    stops and reports (rule 10) — the story was mis-scoped.

15. **Every story states its Impact, right after Gap, in plain language.** One or two sentences a reader
    with no technical background can follow: what was true (the limitation/problem) before this story,
    and what's different after. Not a template — write the actual before/after, e.g. *"Before S17, an
    out-of-window game either served stale data forever or re-fetched from MLB on every view. S17 impact:
    stale games refresh once and cool down, so pages stay current without hammering MLB's servers."*
    This is documentation, not a graded AC — no `scripts/verify-<ID>.sh` checks it — but a [backlog
    review](#backlog-reviews) spot-checks that it exists and isn't jargon-only. It is the raw material for
    the story's `CHANGELOG.md` entry (rule 16); write it so that entry is nearly a copy-paste.

16. **A `done` story updates `CHANGELOG.md` in the same commit as its code (or its ledger entry, for a
    backfilled story).** `CHANGELOG.md` lives at the repo root — it is the **user-facing** counterpart to
    this file: impact-first headlines anyone can read, with a short **Details** line underneath naming the
    story ID (and ADR, if relevant) for readers who want the technical trail. Frame a dev-only change (a
    tooling fix, a coverage floor) by who it benefits and how — trust in the test suite, contributor
    experience — not just what changed. **Nest stories under a bold effort header** only when they are
    clearly part of one larger push that already has a header in the file; do not force nesting on an
    unrelated change. A story whose only outcome is an internal grader-script fix with nothing a reader
    outside the team would call an outcome may skip an entry — default to including one.

17. **The [Current baseline](#current-baseline) moves with the story list.** Any change set that flips a
    story to `done`, or inserts, removes, or re-scopes a story (including inside a backlog review), updates
    the baseline table in the same commit — it lives in `docs/v3/backlog/frame/01 Current baseline.md`;
    edit it there and run `pnpm backlog:build`: the affected rows' **State** (citing the story ID and the
    concrete path/command that now exists) and the **As of** line (date, HEAD it describes, last story
    landed). A row may only say **Done** for something that exists at HEAD — not for what a story promises.
    A backlog review checks the table against HEAD and fixes any row that has drifted.

18. **UI is designed before it is built, and the product owner ratifies the design.** A story that
    builds or restyles a user-facing surface carries a `**Design:**` line naming the design stories
    for that surface (**S31–S34**, or a later one). It may not move to `doing` until every design
    story it names is `done` — `pnpm backlog:check` (in `pnpm lint`, the pre-commit hook, and CI)
    refuses the backlog otherwise. **Drafting is open, ratifying is the owner's** (owner, 2026-10-08):
    the owner or an agent may draft frames in Figma (an agent loads `figma:figma-use` first), but an
    agent never makes a design choice the owner's decisions and VISUAL-DESIGN don't settle — it asks.
    A design story is done only when the surface is **ratified**: `docs/v3/visual/<surface>/RATIFIED.md`
    records who ratified, the date, the source version, the owner's go-ahead quoted verbatim, and a
    SHA-256 manifest of every file it seals. An agent writes `RATIFIED.md` **only when the owner has
    explicitly told it, in the current session, to ratify that surface** — never on an assumed
    go-ahead. Once ratified, sealed files are never edited: a change is an **amendment**,
    `docs/v3/visual/<surface>/amendments/A<N>.md`, which names what it overrides or repeals, carries
    its own frames and manifest, and is ratified the same way. UI stories are written and changed only
    from ratified designs and amendments, through a backlog review, and cite them. A UI story that
    finds its surface needs a screen or state the ratified design doesn't show stops and reports
    rather than designing it in code. Non-UI stories (API, ingest, cache, tooling) carry no
    `**Design:**` line and are not gated.
    **Waiting on the owner does not stall the loop** (added by the 2026-09-14 review; extended to the
    Figma-revision stories S35–S38 on 2026-10-08): a design or Figma-revision story waiting on the
    owner is *parked* — `status: blocked`, `pnpm backlog:build`, and a checkpoint commit of the
    prepared work. That commit satisfies rule 6; `blocked` keeps the gate closed (only `done` opens
    it) and drops the story out of the generated **Next** line, which a `doing` story would otherwise
    hold. A later session sets `doing` to revise or to finish. A design story's turn cap counts agent
    turns across all of its sessions. The generated **Next** line skips `todo` stories whose
    `**Design:**` stories are not all `done` and names the ones it skipped, so it always points at a
    story `backlog:check` will let start.

19. **Every story says what it is for** (owner, 2026-10-09). A `**Source:**` line, right after
    **Impact**, names one of these, in order of preference:
    - `Feature: <name>; <name>` — features [FEATURES](./FEATURES.md) describes (a carry/cut row, a
      product theme, a patronage row). Use this whenever any feature applies.
    - `Pillar: <Name> — <why>. Approved by owner YYYY-MM-DD: "<owner's words>"` — a pillar from
      [INTENT](./INTENT.md#pillars), **only** when no feature applies, and **only** with the owner's
      approval, because a missing feature may be one the owner has in mind but never wrote down. An
      agent writes the approval only when the owner explicitly approved that citation in the current
      session, quoting their words. Approving one story's pillar does not extend to another. A
      material re-scope of the story voids the approval.
    - `Open: <question>. Raised YYYY-MM-DD.` — neither fits. The owner decides: drop the story, describe
      the feature (FEATURES gets it in their words, and the story cites it), or approve a pillar. An
      agent never invents a feature or stretches a pillar to make a story fit.

    When the owner describes a new feature in a session, FEATURES is edited in the same change set as
    the story that cites it. `pnpm backlog:check` (in `pnpm lint`, the pre-commit hook, and CI) refuses a
    story with no `**Source:**` line, a feature FEATURES doesn't name or drops, a pillar INTENT doesn't
    name or the owner hasn't approved, or an `Open` story set to `doing`. The generated **Next** line
    skips `todo` stories with an open question. Whether a citation is *honest* — the feature really
    describes the story, no feature fits a pillar-cited one — is the [doc parity
    review](#doc-parity-reviews)'s check.

20. **Every story has a `**Reuse check**` section** ([ADR-025](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-025--code-that-stays-understandable-comments-and-one-implementation-accepted-2026-10-19), owner, 2026-10-19: *"I would prefer that agents proactively check while they plan their code as well."*). Before planning code, **search existing domain functions, components and hooks** for what the change needs — at least `packages/domain`, `web/src/components/`, `web/src/layout/` and `web/src/api/` — **and record what was reused or why not**. The section sits after the acceptance criteria and names where to look; the agent records the result in the story's commit body as a `Reuse check:` paragraph, because `scripts/audit.sh story` takes no free-text notes. A value derived from BT data that already has a domain function is reused, never re-derived. Before finishing, run `pnpm comments:stale` and re-read every comment it lists (ADR-025: it flags, never fails). `pnpm dup:check` (`jscpd`, in `pnpm verify`) fails on copy-paste; the backlog review's duplication sweep looks for the same meaning written differently. Until `pnpm backlog:check` enforces the section (a `scripts/backlog-vault/` change outside every story fence), the backlog review checks it by hand.
21. **Coverage floors ratchet up, never down** ([ADR-026](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-026--performance-budgets-and-test-coverage-accepted-2026-10-19); owner, 2026-10-19: ratchet). Each package's `vitest.config.ts` floor (lines, branches, functions, statements) sits at its measured value rounded down to the whole percent (set by S54, 2026-10-20). **Each story that adds code raises the floors it can** to the new measured value, rounded down, until the targets hold: **domain 95** lines, **every other package 85 lines / 80 branches**, by the end of the UI band. **A story may never lower a floor**; if it cannot hold one, it stops and reports (rule 10). `packages/ports` is interfaces only and has no floor. The bundle budget sits beside it: `pnpm size` (`size-limit`, `.size-limit.json`, in `pnpm verify` after `pnpm build`) fails when the entry JavaScript passes 200 KB gzipped; heavy views pin their re-render counts with `web/src/test/renderCount.tsx`. **How:** a story that edits a package's code fences that package's `vitest.config.ts` (`packages/*/` fences already include theirs), and before its status flip runs `scripts/verify-S54.sh` and raises every floor its check 3 names (2026-10-25 backlog review: S76 slipped, S77 and S6 passed once a note told them to; every `todo` story's fence now carries the config).

22. **A UI story is checked against its ratified frames by the owner's eye** ([ADR-026](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-026--performance-budgets-and-test-coverage-accepted-2026-10-19), amended 2026-10-28; owner: *"I also want to modify the acceptance critera for the UI stories as you suggested, to compare screenshots to the designs. At least for now. If we have major mismatches consistently, I'll have to revisit."*). Every story with a `**Design:**` line carries an acceptance criterion that, for each ratified frame it builds (every state and pairing drawn), captures the built page in the same state and pairing (Playwright, against fixtures) and records the screenshot beside the frame with the story's ledger entry. "Beside" means paired in the ledger: S81 keeps captures in `docs/v3/design-checks/<ID>/` (the ratified folders are sealed by their manifests), and `scripts/audit.sh story --design-match` records each capture next to its frame, both with SHA-256 (2026-10-28 backlog review). The story may flip to `done` only after the owner has said, in the session, that each pair matches; the ledger quotes the words. No pixel diff (the frames' data differ from the fixtures), and neither the agent nor the grader may declare a match. Waiting on the owner parks the story (`status: blocked`, checkpoint commit), like a design story waiting on ratification. A backlog review places the harness this needs ahead of the first UI story that uses it.

**Status legend:** `todo` · `doing` · `done` · `blocked`

### Verify-script contract

Every `scripts/verify-<ID>.sh` must:

- Exit **0** only when **every** acceptance-criterion check for that story holds; exit **nonzero** otherwise.
- **Report every check, not just the failures.** Source `scripts/lib/checks.sh`; declare each check up front with `check <id> "<description>"`; call `bad <id> "<reason>"` on failure; end with `report "verify-<ID>"` and `exit $?`. That prints one `check <id> PASS|FAIL: <description>` line per declared check plus a tally. A grader that prints only failures leaves no record of what a passing run actually proved, and `scripts/audit.sh` will fall back to recording its exit code alone — which is not an audit.
- Keep the `# --- Check <id>: <description> ---` section comment and the `check <id>` declaration in sync; the declared description is what lands in the ledger.
- **Fail against current HEAD** when the story’s product work does not exist yet (all `todo` stories today). Exception: **S1** is already implemented — its script must **pass** on current HEAD.
- Be deterministic and read-only toward the world: **no network**, **no writes outside the repo**, **no production** Cloudflare (`wrangler deploy`), Neon production branch, Logto production tenant, MLB, or Patreon. It must not write to the working tree (temp dirs under `/tmp` are fine). Localhost to an ephemeral server **started by a story-scoped Vitest file** is allowed; MLB, Firebase prod, and the public internet are not.
- Do its **own** checking. It must **not** invoke `pnpm verify`, repo-wide `pnpm test`, or `pnpm test:coverage`. It may run **named, story-scoped** Vitest files listed in that story’s checks.
- Finish in **under 60 seconds**.
- Be **demonstrated failing on HEAD first** (rule 9). This is a property of the run, not the file: write the script, run it, show the nonzero exit, then implement.

### Backlog reviews

`pnpm verify` proves the code is healthy; it says nothing about whether **this plan** is still right. Re-evaluate the backlog when review debt is due — **6** stories `done` since the last review entry in [AUDIT](./AUDIT.md), **or** any drift event (story count doubled from 3 by the owner, 2026-10-21; single events kept immediate: *"Reduce the single events back to single"*; fence widened, turn cap hit, ACs rewritten mid-run, new ADR accepted, new workspace package, story inserted/re-prioritized outside a review, `pnpm verify` changed). **Applying the owner's answers to a review's own questions is not a drift event**: it is part of finishing that review, logged with `scripts/audit.sh answers backlog --review <date> …`. Only a change that goes beyond what the owner answered counts. Procedure: [`.claude/skills/backlog-review/SKILL.md`](../../.claude/skills/backlog-review/SKILL.md).

Run it with **fresh context** (separate agent/session — an agent that wrote these stories will confirm them), and do not start a story while a review is due. A `continue` verdict must cite the evidence from check 2; a review with no findings and no evidence counts as not having happened.

**The review log lives in [`docs/v3/AUDIT.md`](./AUDIT.md)**, interleaved with the story verification entries that define "6 stories since". Append to it with the script — never by hand:

```bash
scripts/audit.sh review --trigger "…" --since "S23, S21, S13" --verdict amended --findings "…"
```

This section keeps only the *forward-looking* scheduling state: what is due next, and the drift the next review has to weigh.

### Doc parity reviews

A backlog review asks whether the plan is still right against the repo. A **doc parity review** asks whether the product docs still describe what the backlog and the shipped code are: every story's `**Source:**` (rule 19) is honest, every open question is in front of the owner, and [INTENT](./INTENT.md) and [FEATURES](./FEATURES.md) don't contradict what is being built. Otherwise those docs turn into a record of an old plan. Procedure: [`.claude/skills/doc-parity-review/SKILL.md`](../../.claude/skills/doc-parity-review/SKILL.md). Fresh context, as for a backlog review.

**When it is due:** `pnpm parity:debt` reports it from git and [AUDIT](./AUDIT.md), comparing HEAD with the commit that logged the last parity review or the owner's answers to it. It is due when, since then, a product doc (INTENT, ORIGIN, FEATURES, VISUAL-DESIGN, ARCHITECTURE) changed, a story was added or removed, a story's `**Source:**` line changed, a **pillar-cited** story's Gap, Impact or acceptance criteria changed (the owner's approval may no longer cover it), or **6** stories went `done`. Any single listed change makes it due; only the story count was doubled (owner, 2026-10-21). Other story-text edits don't count: a feature citation is checked against FEATURES, not the story text, and a pillar story's scope list, goal-line paths, work items or notes don't change what it is for (owner, 2026-10-23), so most backlog reviews don't make a parity review due. Do not start a story while it is due.

**Why the reviews don't keep setting each other off** (corrected 2026-10-09: the first version of this list held up for the reviews' own edits, but missed the loop that actually fired — a review asked the owner a question, applying the answer counted as drift, and that made another review due):

1. **Answering a review finishes it.** When a review asks the owner questions, applying the answers is logged as that review's **answers** entry (`scripts/audit.sh answers backlog|parity --review <date> --commit <sha> --answers -`), quoting the owner. The debt checks measure from it, as from the review. Only changes beyond what the owner answered count as drift.
2. **Separate write scopes.** A parity review edits only INTENT and FEATURES, plus stories' `**Source:**` lines, and only to record a decision the owner has already made (a quote, a story they asked for, a commit), citing it. A backlog review never edits INTENT, FEATURES, or a `**Source:**` line, except on a story it inserts, which still has to pass rule 19.
3. **A review doesn't trigger itself.** Parity debt is measured from the commit that logged the last parity review, and that review commits its edits in that same commit. Its own work is never counted as drift.
4. **A parity review never causes a backlog drift event.** It doesn't insert, re-prioritize, or re-scope stories, accept ADRs, or touch `pnpm verify`. When it finds backlog work (a FEATURES item no story owns, say), it writes the finding into its ledger entry under **For the next backlog review**, and that review must answer it. A backlog review makes a parity review due only when it adds or removes a story, or re-scopes a pillar-cited one, and never the other way round.
5. **Only the owner decides product.** Where a doc and the backlog disagree and no recorded decision settles which is right, the verdict is `blocked` and the owner is asked.

```bash
pnpm parity:debt                                   # is a parity review due, and why
scripts/audit.sh parity --trigger "…" --verdict amended --findings -
scripts/audit.sh answers parity --review <date> --commit <sha> --answers -   # owner's answers to that review
```

### Goal command for multiple stories

```/goal docs/v3/BACKLOG.md SX then SY. Follow the Rules for every story, plus each story's Goal condition and Turn cap as written — in particular rule 9 (show me each grader failing on HEAD before product code), rule 10 (stop and report rather than widening a fence), and rule 6 (do not start a story until the work for the prior story is committed). Stop after <SX cap + SY cap> turns total.```

| Versioned, idempotent updates (ADR-022) | **Partial** — the rules exist in `packages/domain`: `applyIfNewer` (`versioning.ts`) and `contentHash` (`content-hash.ts`) (**S43**). `GameSnapshot` / `ScheduleDay` carry `version` + `lastChangedAt` on the wire, stamped by `stampVersion` (bumps only when `contentHash` changes), and every repository applies an upsert only if its version is newer (**S46**). The hub and client cache don't apply it yet (**S48** / **S19**) |
| Cache freshness (ADR-021) | **Partial** — `cacheLifetimeMs` + ladder constants in `packages/domain/src/cache-lifetime.ts` (**S43**); callers still use the fixed `CACHE_TTL_MS` 5 min in `services/refresh.ts` and send no `Cache-Control` headers until **S47** |
| Representative local dev (`pnpm dev` vs deployed) | **Partial** — `pnpm dev` is zero-setup (local API :8787 + Vite :5173, in-memory repos, fixtures). Owner, 2026-10-18: the most standard representative option — **S51** moves `pnpm dev` onto Postgres in Docker (after **S45** / **S50**) |
| Personal data: inventory and deletion (ADR-028) | **Partial** — inventory and checks (**S76**): `PersonalDataStore` in `packages/ports`; `personalDataStores(deps)` registers `BT database: users`; the classification manifest `functions/src/services/data-classification.ts` (kinds `personal` / `none` / `retained`, `retained` only on the deletion log) fails on anything unlabeled; repository contract case (h); `bt/no-browser-storage` keeps browser storage in `web/src/storage/`, whose `clearPersonalData()` runs on sign-out. Deletion API (**S77**, re-scoped by **S80**): `POST /api/v1/me/delete` needs a sign-in from the last 10 minutes and `ACCOUNT_DELETION_PHRASE` (`packages/domain`) exactly, no download, then deletes from every store and `IdentityAdmin` (dev: `DevIdentityAdmin`), `BT database: users` last so a failed attempt retries; `InMemoryDeletionLog` keeps uid + time and `reapplyDeletions` re-applies it after a restore; routes reach an account only through `authenticateAccount`; request bodies come from `ApiRequestBodies` (spec `requestBody`); `services/signed-token.ts` is the one HMAC helper (sessions). Downloads (**S80**): `POST /api/v1/me/download` walks the registry into an `ExportStore` (`packages/ports`) download that ages out after 14 days (`downloadExpiresAt`), refused with 429 and `nextAllowedAt` past two in rolling 24 hours (`nextDownloadAllowedAt`), and sends one email through `Mailer` linking to `<BT_APP_ORIGIN>/settings` (none without an address); `GET /api/v1/me/download` and `/:downloadId` read the current download and its file, owner only, 404 otherwise; `InMemoryExportStore` (exports records, never files) and `InMemoryMailer` are registered as `Cloud storage: data downloads` and `Cloudflare Email` and deleted with the account. Settings store (**S6**): `BT database: settings` registered beside `BT database: users` and labeled personal; the store-generic deletion contract case (i) runs for both. Still to come: R2 and Cloudflare Email adapters (S45 and the deploy theme), **S78** design, **S79** Settings flow; S50 registers its tables, S74 keeps `/api/v1/me` out of the offline cache |
| Multi-source deep links / AI / push (Web Push, ADR-017) | Not started |

## Stories

> **Route paths and ADR-015.** Stories authored before [ADR-015](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-015--api-versioning--compatibility-accepted) name unversioned routes (`/api/schedule`, `/api/games/:gamePk`, …). Once **S26** lands the `/api/v1` prefix, every such literal means its **`/api/v1/…`** equivalent — in the story text, in each `scripts/verify-<ID>.sh`, and in any new route a later story adds. A story that introduces a route on an unversioned path after S26 is wrong, not a permitted exception.

With enforcement now real, `@bt/functions` fails its own `branches` floor: 54.07% measured against a declared 60% (`functions/vitest.config.ts`). The review temporarily lowered that number to 50 so `pnpm verify` is green again; that is debt, not a decision to run the package at a lower bar. The gap is concentrated in already-shipped pure mapper functions — `mappers/live.ts` (12.85% branch, 70 total branches) and `mappers/schedule.ts` (19.04%, 21 total branches) account for most of the ~152 uncovered branches, with smaller gaps in `mappers/content.ts`, `mappers/standings.ts`, `mappers/players.ts`, `services/recorder.ts`, and `handlers/api.ts`.

### S26 — Typed BT API route contract

**Gap:** The response type is unbound at **both** ends of the wire, and routes are unversioned. Egress: `sendJson(res: ServerResponse, status: number, body: unknown)` in `functions/src/handlers/api.ts` erases the type, and nothing declares that `/api/games/:gamePk` returns a `GameSnapshot` — a handler can return the wrong shape and still typecheck. Ingress: `getJson<T>` in `web/src/api/client.ts` lets each caller assert whatever type it wants. Both sides import `@bt/domain`, so the *types* are shared, but no typechecked contract ties a route to its response.

**Impact:** Before S26, nothing actually checked that an API endpoint sent the shape of data it claimed to, and routes had no version number. S26 impact: a mismatch between what an endpoint sends and what a page expects is now caught before the code ever ships, and every route carries a version so a future change can't silently break something still depending on the old shape.

**Source:** Pillar: Dependable — a mismatch between what an API route sends and what a page expects is caught before it ships. Approved by owner 2026-10-09: "The rest are all fine."

**Why here:** [ADR-014](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-014--client-state-management-accepted) requires data typed up to egress and typed again immediately on ingress, from one declaration. **S25** builds the query cache on top of that contract, so this lands first — otherwise the cache's payload types are asserted rather than derived. **S27** generates the OpenAPI spec by walking this table, which is why the table must be runtime-enumerable here. Independently valuable: it types today's two handlers before any cache exists.

**Why the version prefix lands now:** [ADR-015](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-015--api-versioning--compatibility-accepted) — versioning cannot be retrofitted without breaking. Once clients call `/api/schedule`, adding `/api/v1/schedule` *is* the breaking change. One path segment now buys the option permanently.

**Accepted scope of the guarantee:** JSON on the wire is untyped (a limitation of the medium). This story makes the boundary **statically** bound; it does **not** add runtime validation, and it does **not** make anything schema-first.

**Response aliases (2026-09-13, ADR-014 amended):** each route's response type is a named `<DomainType>Response` alias of its `@bt/domain` source — `GameSnapshotResponse`, `ScheduleDayResponse` — not the domain type referenced directly, sent through a `to<DomainType>Response` mapping function that is a **passthrough today**. This is the seam for decoupling the wire contract from internal domain evolution later (a real external consumer, an app in another language) without paying for a full DTO catalog now — see [ADR-014 §Response aliases](./ARCHITECTURE.md#response-aliases--the-dto-seam-accepted-2026-09-13). It is a naming and indirection change only: the alias is structurally identical to its domain type, so this does not reopen the "one type source" drift risk ADR-014 rule 9 forbids.

**Depends on:** S21 (so the contract names the BT store shapes, not pass-through snapshots)

**Scope files:** `packages/domain/`, `functions/src/`, `web/`, `firebase.json`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S26.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S26.sh` performs)

1. **One** shared module under `packages/domain/src/` declares the route table (exported name contains `ApiRoutes`) as a **runtime-enumerable `as const` value** — not a type alone — covering at minimum `GET /api/v1/schedule` → `ScheduleDayResponse` and `GET /api/v1/games/:gamePk` → `GameSnapshotResponse`, plus a named `<Name>Response` error-body type used by the 400/404 paths. Each entry's response type is bound through a `keyof`-constrained registry, so an unknown type key is a compile error (no unenforced string keys).
1a. Each `<DomainType>Response` used in the table is declared beside it (same module or one it re-exports) as `export type <DomainType>Response = <DomainType>;` — an alias, not an independently hand-written shape. The script greps for at least two exported type names matching `*Response` whose right-hand side is the bare domain type name.
1b. **Every** route path in the table begins `/api/v1/`, and the script fails if any unversioned `"/api/<name>"` route literal remains in `functions/src/handlers/api.ts`, `web/src/`, or `web/vite.config.ts` proxy config.
1c. A type-level assertion proves each response alias is mutually assignable with its domain type today (both directions — e.g. a value typed as the domain type is assignable to the alias and back). Checked by the same `tsc --noEmit` run as check 3. This is what makes a future divergence a deliberate, visible edit to the mapping function (check 2) rather than silent drift.
2. Egress is typed: `functions/src/handlers/api.ts` no longer declares `body: unknown` on success responses, sends each route's payload through a matching `to<DomainType>Response` mapping function (the script greps for at least two `to*Response(` call sites), and its JSON sender is generic over the table (grep for the table's exported name in that file). Each mapping function is a **passthrough** today (`return value;` or equivalent) — no field renaming yet.
3. A **server** type-level test proves a wrong-shaped response fails typecheck: it contains `@ts-expect-error` on a bad send for a known route, and `pnpm --filter @bt/functions exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` exits **0** (an unnecessary `@ts-expect-error` would make `tsc` fail, so exit 0 proves the binding is real).
4. Ingress is typed: `web/src/api/client.ts` exposes a fetch helper keyed by the route map, and **no** call site under `web/src/` passes a type argument (grep finds no `getJson<`).
5. Exactly **one** type assertion exists in the ingress path: `web/src/api/client.ts` contains at most **1** occurrence of `as ` / `as unknown as`, and no other file under `web/src/api/` contains one.
6. A **client** type-level test proves the derived type is enforced: `@ts-expect-error` on assigning a route's response to a wrong type, with `pnpm --filter @bt/web exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` exiting **0**.
7. **No runtime validation added** at this boundary (recording the ADR-014 decision): the script greps `functions/src/handlers/api.ts` and `web/src/api/` and fails if `zod` or `valibot` is imported. `@bt/mlb-api` parsers are untouched and out of scope.
8. `pnpm --filter @bt/functions exec vitest run src/handlers/api.test.ts` exits 0 (existing API behavior unchanged).
9. This file's S26 **Status** (story heading and top table) is `done`.

**Out of scope**

- The query cache itself (S25).
- Runtime response validation, and any schema-first rewrite of BT store shapes — explicitly rejected in ADR-014.
- New routes. This story types the routes that exist; S4/S5/S13 add their own entries to the map when they land.
- Making any `<DomainType>Response` alias actually diverge from its domain type. The mapping functions are passthroughs; a real DTO catalog is a later story if a real external consumer ever shows up (ADR-014 §Response aliases).

**Needs human judgment**

- Whether the map's ergonomics hold up as routes with params multiply (the script only checks the two current routes are bound).

**Goal condition:** scripts/verify-S26.sh exits 0, pnpm verify exits 0, no files outside packages/domain/, functions/src/, web/, firebase.json, docs/v3/BACKLOG.md, docs/v3/AUDIT.md, CHANGELOG.md are modified, no files under scripts/ or test/ are modified, or stop after 16 turns. If a criterion cannot be met inside that path list, stop and report which criterion and which path — do not widen the scope yourself.

**Turn cap:** 16 — assumes one route table, one typed sender, one typed fetch helper, two type-level tests, the `/api/v1` path move, and no new routes. Was 12 before ADR-015 added the version prefix (which touches the handler paths, the Vite proxy, and existing call sites); raised 14 → 16 for the 2026-09-13 response-alias amendment — two type aliases, two passthrough mapping functions, and one more type-level assertion, each small but real. If typing the existing handlers forces layout changes under `web/src/pages/`, stop and report: that is S25's job.

### S27 — OpenAPI spec generated from the contract + oasdiff gate

**Gap:** Nothing describes the BT API outside TypeScript, and nothing mechanically blocks a backward-incompatible change. [ADR-015](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-015--api-versioning--compatibility-accepted) makes additive-only within a version the rule; without a gate it is a wish.

**Impact:** Before S27, there was no description of the app's API outside its own source code, and nothing stopped a change from silently breaking anyone relying on it. S27 impact: a machine-readable spec is generated automatically from the real API, and a check blocks any change that would break compatibility for existing clients.

**Source:** Pillar: Dependable — a breaking change to the API is caught by a gate instead of breaking clients. Approved by owner 2026-10-09: "The rest are all fine."

**Why here:** Directly after **S26**, because the spec is generated by walking that story's runtime route table. Landing it before the UI fill stories means every route added later (S4 standings, S5 search, S13) is gated from birth.

**Why it survived the 2026-09-13 re-decision** (the counterfactual two prior reviews carried): S26's typed contract catches a server/client **disagreement**, not a **backward-incompatible change**. Change a domain type and its consuming page in the same commit and `pnpm verify` is green while the wire contract has broken for anyone not redeployed with it. A diff against a committed baseline is the only mechanism in this plan that catches that class, so S27 is not a duplicate of the typecheck. It is also the only artifact a non-TypeScript consumer can read — which the product owner raised directly on 2026-09-13 ("what if I did want to add, for example, an app? Or offer my API to others?"). See [Backlog reviews](#backlog-reviews) for the full argument.

**Single source:** the spec is a **derived artifact**, never hand-edited. The TypeScript contract stays authoritative — this story adds no second source of truth and no runtime validation.

**Source types are the response aliases, not the domain types (2026-09-13 review).** [ADR-014's response-alias seam](./ARCHITECTURE.md#response-aliases--the-dto-seam-accepted-2026-09-13) means the wire type is `GameSnapshotResponse` / `ScheduleDayResponse`, not `GameSnapshot` / `ScheduleDay`. The `ApiRoutes` table's *values* are already those alias names (`"GET /api/v1/games/:gamePk": "GameSnapshotResponse"`), so the emitter generates a schema per alias name it reads from the table. Generating from the bare domain type instead would make the spec describe the wrong thing the moment a `to<DomainType>Response` mapping function stops being a passthrough — silently, since nothing would fail.

**Depends on:** S26 (`done`)

**Scope files:** `packages/domain/`, `functions/`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `openapi/`, `.github/workflows/`, `README.md`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S27.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S27.sh` performs)

1. A generator entrypoint exists under `functions/` or `packages/` (**not** `scripts/`), wired to a root `package.json` script such as `api:spec`. It uses **`ts-json-schema-generator`** for response schemas and an in-repo emitter that walks the S26 route table. `ts-oas` is **not** used (ADR-015 rejects it: it would dictate domain type shapes).
1a. **The emitter's schema type names come from the route table's values** — the `<DomainType>Response` aliases (`ScheduleDayResponse`, `GameSnapshotResponse`, `ApiErrorResponse`), not the bare `@bt/domain` types. The script greps the emitter source and fails if a response schema is requested for `GameSnapshot` or `ScheduleDay` by name rather than through the table. (Rationale under **Source types** above.)
2. The generated spec is committed at `openapi/bt-api.v1.json` (or `.yaml`), is valid JSON/YAML, declares `openapi: 3.x`, and contains a path entry for **every** route in the S26 table — the script cross-checks the table's route count against the spec's operation count.
3. Each operation's success response `$ref`s a component schema named for that route's alias, whose properties include the payload's fields (the script spot-checks `fetchedAt` and `windowMode`, both of which exist on `GameSnapshot` and `ScheduleDay` at HEAD).
3a. **Error responses are in the spec.** Every operation declares at least one 4xx response `$ref`ing a component schema generated from `ApiErrorResponse` (`error: string`, `hint?: string`), and the schedule operation declares `400` while the game operation declares `404` — matching `functions/src/handlers/api.ts` today. **Note:** the S26 `ApiRoutes` table maps route → *success* type only and carries no status codes, so the emitter supplies the status-code mapping. If a route ever needs an error body other than `ApiErrorResponse`, the table has to grow — stop and report; that is a new story, not a widen.
4. **The spec is not stale:** re-running the generator into a temp dir produces a file byte-identical to the committed one (the script regenerates and diffs). No network.
5. `oasdiff` is available as a repo dev dependency (`oasdiff-js` or a pinned binary) and a root script such as `api:breaking` runs it with `--fail-on ERR`. **The baseline is an explicitly named committed file distinct from the generated spec** — `openapi/bt-api.v1.baseline.json` — so the gate is never a self-diff (a spec compared against itself is always clean and proves nothing). `api:breaking` diffs the freshly generated spec against that baseline. The script fails if `api:breaking` resolves both sides to the same path.
6. The gate is proven to work in **both** directions, offline, by a named test or the script itself: an unmodified spec → exit 0; a spec fixture with a **removed response field** → nonzero with a breaking-change finding. The mutated fixture lives in a temp dir, not in `openapi/`.
7. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the spec-freshness check and the breaking-change gate. CI stays offline — the script fails if the workflow adds a step that fetches a spec over the network.
8. `README.md` documents: regenerate with `pnpm api:spec`, the spec is generated and never hand-edited, additive-only within `v1`, a breaking change means a new version per ADR-015, and **how the baseline is advanced** — a deliberate, reviewed edit accompanying an additive change, never an automatic copy of the generated spec (an auto-advancing baseline is a disabled gate).
9. This file's S27 **Status** (story heading and top table) is `done`.

**Out of scope**

- Publishing the spec anywhere (docs site, Swagger UI) — ADR-015 "Still open".
- Client or server code generated *from* the spec. Generation flows one way: TypeScript → spec.
- Runtime request/response validation (rejected in ADR-014).
- Creating a v2, or multi-version mounting (ADR-015 non-goal until v2 exists).
- Semantic breaking changes — a field whose meaning changes while its shape does not. ADR-015 names this as unreachable by tooling; do not claim the gate covers it.

**Needs human judgment**

- Whether `oasdiff` severity tuning (which `WARN`s to promote to `ERR`) matches how the team wants to be interrupted.
- Whether the emitter's operation ids, descriptions, and error responses are good enough to hand to a human reader.

If a criterion cannot be met inside that path list, stop and report which criterion and which path — do not widen the scope yourself.

### S29 — Generated response types + spec-fidelity gate

**Gap:** S27 commits `openapi/bt-api.v1.json` as a derived artifact that **nothing consumes**. `oasdiff` only compares the spec against its own previous self, never against reality — so a route the emitter under-specifies (a dropped field, wrong nullability, a widened union) passes the gate forever and stays wrong. Nothing forces the spec to be right, and the README tells readers it is.

**Impact:** Before S29, the API description generated by S27 had nothing checking it against the real code, so an inaccuracy could sit there undetected and still be trusted. S29 impact: the app's own build reads that description back and fails if it no longer matches the real data shapes — so the published description cannot quietly drift away from what the server actually sends.

**Source:** Pillar: Dependable — the generated API spec is checked against the real code, so it can be trusted. Approved by owner 2026-10-09: "The rest are all fine."

**Why here:** After **S27** (needs the committed spec) and — as of the 2026-09-13 review — **after S25** rather than before it. [ADR-016](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-016--generated-client-dal-from-the-openapi-spec-accepted) records the round-trip decision and the fidelity guard that makes it acceptable; this story is now scoped to **that guard**, with the DAL adoption deferred (below).

**Why it moved behind S25 (2026-09-13 review).** ADR-016's own honest accounting says this story "buys exactly one thing: proof that the spec is faithful" — it is a **check on S27's emitter**, not a product capability, and it blocks nothing. S25 blocks eight stories. The original ordering ("before S25, so the cache isn't built on an ingress layer this story would immediately replace") overstated the rework: S25's resource modules derive payload types through `ApiResponseFor`, so the swap is an import change in two files inside this story's existing `web/` fence, not a rewrite.

**Re-decided 2026-09-16 (backlog review) — split, not deferred wholesale.** The standing re-decision the 2026-09-13 review required was carried out against `dafeae8`. Its finding: the two halves of this story have very different value.

- **The guard is the part worth having, and it does not need the DAL.** ADR-016's own accounting says the round-trip "buys exactly one thing: proof that the spec is faithful." That proof is produced by generating *types* from the committed spec and asserting mutual assignability — no `openapi-fetch`, no fetch-layer rewrite. The guard is what makes deferring the rest safe, because it turns "does the wire type space still round-trip losslessly?" from a grep a reviewer has to remember into a compile error.
- **The DAL adoption is the part that buys nothing today, and it is deferred.** `openapi-fetch`, and purging the hand-written route-path literals from `web/src/api/client.ts`, move to the **Generated DAL adoption** Later theme behind a named trigger. There is no external consumer (FEATURES drops public catalog APIs; ADR-016's own "Still open" is exactly whether one ever justifies publishing the spec), and a typed fetch wrapper duplicates what the S26 route key already does for the response type.
- **The prior review's stated risk did not survive contact with the emitter.** It kept this story partly because "68 `| null` unions … nullable representation is exactly where JSON Schema → OpenAPI → TS loses fidelity." At HEAD the emitter represents nullability in OpenAPI 3.1's native forms — `{"type": ["string","null"]}` and `anyOf: [$ref, {"type":"null"}]` — both of which `openapi-typescript` reverses exactly. Expect AC 4 to pass first try; that is the point of the reduced cap, not a reason to skip it.

**Depends on:** S26 (runtime-enumerable route table, `done`), S27 (committed spec + `oasdiff` gate), S25 (the resource modules whose payload-type imports this story swaps)

**Scope files:** `web/`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Note on the generator command:** it must be a `package.json` script (or config under `web/`), **not** a new file under `scripts/` — that directory is frozen after work item 0.

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S29.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S29.sh` performs)

1. `web/package.json` depends on `openapi-typescript`. A `package.json` script regenerates the types from the committed spec **with no network** (the grader runs it offline). **`openapi-fetch` is deliberately *not* added** (re-scoped 2026-09-16 — see the Later theme); the script fails if it appears in any manifest.
2. Generated output lives under `web/src/api/generated/`, is committed, and every file there carries an `@generated` banner in its first 5 lines. The script fails if any file in that directory lacks one.
3. **Drift gate:** running the generator produces **no diff** under `web/src/api/generated/` (`git diff --exit-code` on that path). A stale committed artifact fails the story. This regenerate-then-compare check **also runs as a `web/` Vitest test** (in `pnpm verify` / `pnpm test:coverage`'s path), because ADR-016 requires spec→client freshness *enforced in CI* and both `scripts/` and `.github/` are outside this story's fence — the per-story grader is not a CI gate (`ci.yml` runs lint / test:coverage / build only).
4. **Fidelity gate (the load-bearing check):** a type-level test asserts that for **every** route in the S26 table, the generated response type and that route's **`<DomainType>Response` alias** (`GameSnapshotResponse`, `ScheduleDayResponse` — the type actually on the wire) are **mutually assignable** (assignable both directions, not merely compatible one way). `pnpm --filter @bt/web exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` exits **0**. This is what catches round-trip fidelity loss; without it the story is not done. **Compare against the alias, not the bare `@bt/domain` type** (amended 2026-09-13): the aliases are structurally identical to their domain types today, so the check is equivalent right now — but asserting against `GameSnapshot` directly would, the day a `to<DomainType>Response` mapping function stops being a passthrough, force the alias back into lockstep with the domain type and destroy the [ADR-014 response-alias seam](./ARCHITECTURE.md#response-aliases--the-dto-seam-accepted-2026-09-13) this gate is supposed to protect.
4a. The gate is proven to have teeth, not just to pass: the same type-level test file contains at least one `@ts-expect-error` case showing a deliberately wrong pairing (e.g. the game route's generated type against `ScheduleDayResponse`) fails assignability. An unnecessary `@ts-expect-error` makes `tsc` fail, so AC 4's exit 0 then proves the assertion is real rather than vacuously satisfied by a widened `any`-ish generated type.
5. **The generated types are load-bearing in shipped code, not only in a test.** **S25's resource modules** (`web/src/api/game.ts`, `web/src/api/schedule.ts`) import their payload types from `web/src/api/generated/` rather than through `ApiResponseFor`, completing the forward obligation S25 AC 3 records; the script greps both files for a `generated/` import and fails if either still routes through `ApiResponseFor`. **Re-scoped 2026-09-16:** the other half of the old AC 5 — purging hand-written route-path literals from `web/src/api/client.ts` and routing fetches through `openapi-fetch` — moved to the **Generated DAL adoption** Later theme. Do **not** rewrite `client.ts`'s fetch layer or `client.test.ts` here.
5a. **Generated code is excluded from the `web` coverage floor, and no threshold is lowered.** `web/vitest.config.ts` excludes `src/api/generated/**` from `coverage.exclude` (or narrows `coverage.include`), and its `lines`/`statements`/`functions`/`branches` numbers are **greater than or equal to** the values at the commit that starts this story. Committed generated output is not ours to test; the correct response is to stop counting it, never to drop a floor to accommodate it. The script compares the config's numbers against the story-start commit and fails on any decrease.
6. Grep of `web/src/api/` **excluding** `generated/` finds no `: any`, `as any`, `any[]`, or `as unknown as`.
7. **No runtime validation** added at this boundary (ADR-014 and ADR-016 both reject it): no `zod` or `valibot` import under `web/src/api/`.
8. `pnpm --filter @bt/web exec vitest run` exits 0 (existing web tests still pass).
9. This file's S29 **Status** (story heading and top table) is `done`.

**Out of scope**

- The query cache, its descriptors, its freshness policy, and the page migrations — **S25** owns all of those and now runs **first**. This story only swaps where S25's two resource modules get their payload types from (AC 5); it does not change cache keys, hooks, or any page.
- **The fetch layer.** `openapi-fetch`, the route-path-literal purge in `web/src/api/client.ts`, and the `client.test.ts` rework belong to the **Generated DAL adoption** Later theme, not here.
- Generating **query hooks** (ADR-016 rejects Orval for exactly this reason).
- Generating the **server** from the spec. The route table stays the origin.
- Fixing the emitter. If the fidelity gate in AC 4 fails because the spec genuinely under-specifies a route, that is **S27's** bug — stop and report it rather than patching the generated output or loosening the assertion.

**Needs human judgment**

- Whether the fidelity assertion should stay exhaustive over the route table, or move to a sampled set if the table grows large.
- Whether the regenerate-then-compare Vitest test (AC 3) is fast enough to sit inside `pnpm test:coverage`, or wants a different home once the spec grows.

**Goal condition:** scripts/verify-S29.sh exits 0, pnpm verify exits 0, no files outside web/, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, docs/v3/BACKLOG.md, docs/v3/backlog/, docs/v3/AUDIT.md, CHANGELOG.md are modified, no files under scripts/ or test/ are modified, or stop after 12 turns. If a criterion cannot be met inside that path list, stop and report which criterion and which path — do not widen the scope yourself.

Lowered 18 → 12 by the 2026-09-16 review, which moved `openapi-fetch`, the route-literal purge and the `client.ts`/`client.test.ts` rework out to a Later theme — those were the bulk of the 16 → 18 raise. Assumes **no** page migrations, no cache changes, and no fetch-layer rewrite. If the spec under-specifies a route and AC 4 cannot pass without changing the emitter, stop and report — that is a different story. ### S25 — Typed client query cache (ADR-014 foundation)

**Gap:** Every page hand-rolls `useState` + `useEffect` + `fetch` + a `cancelled` flag ([web/src/pages/GamePage.tsx](../../web/src/pages/GamePage.tsx), [web/src/pages/ScoreboardPage.tsx](../../web/src/pages/ScoreboardPage.tsx)); `web/src/api/client.ts` is two bare functions. There is no cache, no dedup, and **no way to patch a loaded entity in place** — which S19/S20 both require and [VISUAL-DESIGN D7](./VISUAL-DESIGN.md#1-design-goals) mandates. [ADR-014](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-014--client-state-management-accepted) settles the strategy; this story lands the foundation for the **server read cache** kind only.

**Impact:** Before S25, every page fetched its own data independently with no shared cache — the same game could be fetched twice, and there was no way to update what's on screen without a full reload. S25 impact: pages share one typed cache that can be updated in place, the groundwork live updates need so a screen refreshes without losing where you were.

**Source:** Feature: Game → Live play / linescore context; Daily scoreboard by date

**Why here:** After **S21** so cache keys mirror real BT store shapes rather than pass-through `GameSnapshot`, after **S24** so the migrated pages inherit the brand theme, and after **S26** so descriptors derive their payload types from the route contract instead of asserting them. **Before S2–S5** so four new surfaces consume the cache instead of adding four more `useEffect` fetchers, and **before S18–S20** so live delivery has a typed cache-write seam instead of inventing one.

**Moved ahead of S29 (2026-09-13 review).** S25 was previously blocked behind S29 for one reason only — AC 3's requirement that descriptors derive their payload type from `web/src/api/generated/`. S26 now supplies an equivalent derived, route-bound type (`ApiResponseFor<"GET /api/v1/games/:gamePk">`), which satisfies [ADR-014](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-014--client-state-management-accepted) rule 9's "no hand-written server shape in `web/`" just as well. S25 unblocks **eight** stories (S2, S3, S4, S5, S10, S18, S19, S20); S29 unblocks none. Making eight stories wait behind a codegen fidelity loop violates rule 4. AC 3 is rewritten below; **S29 owns flipping the import** to the generated client when it lands (its fence already covers `web/`).

**Depends on:** S26 (route contract — `ApiResponseFor` is the descriptors' payload-type source), S21 (store shapes), S24 (theme). **All `done`.** No longer waits on the generated client DAL — see **Moved ahead** above.

**Scope files:** `web/`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S25.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S25.sh` performs)

2. `web/src/api/` has **one file per resource** — at minimum `game.ts` and `schedule.ts` — and each exports a **`queryOptions(`** descriptor plus a hook named `useGame` / `useScheduleDay` (grep each file).
3. Those descriptors **derive** their payload type from the **S26 route contract** — each resource file's payload type resolves through `ApiResponseFor<"GET /api/v1/…">` (via `web/src/api/client.ts` or a direct `@bt/domain` import of `ApiResponseFor`), never a locally written shape and never a bare `GameSnapshot` / `ScheduleDay` import that bypasses the route binding. The script greps each resource file for `ApiResponseFor` (directly or through the helper it re-exports). **No** file under `web/src/` declares an `interface` or `type` body containing `windowMode` or `fetchedAt` — server shapes are not re-declared client-side (ADR-014 rule 9). **Forward obligation:** [ADR-016](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-016--generated-client-dal-from-the-openapi-spec-accepted) makes `web/src/api/generated/` the eventual ingress-type source; **S29** owns swapping these imports over and tightening this check, and its AC 5 already forbids hand-written route literals outside `generated/`.

**Re-scoped by the 2026-10-19 design intake review:** adds the batting columns and team-color dots the ratified Box frames draw, the unplayed-inning cells, and moves inning arithmetic into `packages/domain` (ADR-025).

### S41 — Plays room — inning sidebar, at-bat accordions, scoring plays

**Gap:** S33 ratified a redesigned Plays room on 2026-10-14 (owner: "Plays is basically like browsing a list of the individual batters in Live … you need to be able to select the inning you're looking at. By default, it should show the most recent inning that has any actual information to show. It needs a floating sidebar showing all of the innings in order. Opening an inning shows the top and bottom of the inning with expandable at-bat accordion items. It also needs an option to show all scoring plays"). At HEAD the Plays tab is the pre-design baseline: `web/src/components/pitch/PlaysPanel.tsx` renders every at-bat of the game as one flat accordion with the first one open. No story builds the ratified room — the S33 DESIGN.md "Work required" says only "built with S2/S3 in the shared game route", and neither story's ACs carry it (the gap map has said since 2026-09-14 that a Plays restyle needs its own story). Inserted by the 2026-10-14 backlog review.

**Impact:** Before S41, the Plays tab was one long list of every at-bat in the game, opening at the first pitch of the first inning. S41 impact: Plays opens on the latest inning that has something to show, a sidebar jumps to any inning or to every scoring play of the game, and each at-bat opens to the same pitch-by-pitch view as Live, with pitches colored ball / strike / in play.

**Re-scoped by the 2026-10-19 design intake review:** the pitcher / batter cards drawn in the expanded at-bat are now in scope (they were excluded); the pitch list and cards become the single components Live (S64) reuses; derivations move to `packages/domain` (ADR-025). Card totals run up to that at-bat (owner, 2026-10-19).

**Source:** Feature: Game → Plays + pitch detail

**Design:** S32, S33 — build to the approved frames in `docs/v3/visual/game-rooms/` (`plays-mobile`, `plays-medium`, `plays-desktop`, `plays-scoring-mobile`) under the chrome in `docs/v3/visual/game-shell/`. This story may only move to `doing` once every design story named here is `done` (rule 18; `pnpm backlog:check` enforces it).

**Depends on:** **S40** (game chrome and phase-aware tabs), **S2** (the boxed-inning linescore component and the per-inning `linescore.innings` data it adds), **S39** (the `pitch/*` color roles). Also **S81** (design capture harness, rule 22).

### S9 — Representative local dev: `pnpm dev` on the Firestore emulator

**Superseded 2026-10-18** (never started) by [ADR-017](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-017--platform-cloudflare-workers--neon-postgres-accepted-2026-10-18): the Firestore emulator workflow it set up is gone. Its storage-contract cases moved to **S46**, its representative-local-dev requirement to **S51**.

**Gap:** Production is meant to store schedules and games in Firestore through the S7 adapter, but nothing has ever run that adapter against Firestore. The repo has no Firebase CLI, no script starts the emulator, this machine has no Java runtime (checked 2026-10-09), and S7's emulator round-trip is skipped in every run. `pnpm dev` uses the in-memory repositories, which behave differently from Firestore: they hand back the very object they stored, while Firestore returns a JSON-plain copy. A feature can therefore pass every local check and fail once deployed. `local-server.ts` runs `main()` on import, so the composition `pnpm dev` actually runs has no test. ADR-013 already says `pnpm dev` runs on the emulators; the code never did.

**Impact:** Before S9, local development "worked", but on storage that behaves differently from production. Nothing proved that a feature working on a laptop would also work deployed. S9 impact: `pnpm dev` runs the app against Google's local copy of the real database, with no cloud account and nothing deployed, so working locally becomes a reliable sign of working in production.

**Source:** Pillar: Delightful — for developers too: local development works without serious setup or a deployed cloud environment, and is representative enough that a feature that works locally very likely works deployed. Approved by owner 2026-10-09: "Delightful. It applies to developers as well, and a local development experience that requires serious setup is a pain in the ass."

**Owner's requirements (2026-10-09, verbatim):** local development *"works, doesn't require its own serverless architecture that has to be deployed just for testing, and … is representative in such a way that a feature which works locally is very likely to work after being deployed"*. *"pnpm dev should be the canonical development path for running locally. If emulators are important for that, it should use emulators."* Then, having weighed a separate in-memory dev command: *"ditch the in-memory one and go emulator-only."* The owner also confirmed the Delightful approval covers this re-scope, and that CI does **not** run the emulator.

**Approach (one path):**

- **`pnpm dev` is the only way to run the app locally.** It starts the Firestore emulator under a `demo-` project ID (no real Firebase project, no login, nothing deployed), seeds it from `fixtures/` on startup, and runs the API and web against it. Data starts fresh each run. The one prerequisite is a Java runtime, which the emulator needs.
- **There is no in-memory way to run the app.** The in-memory repositories stay only as **test doubles** for the fast `functions` tests (CI has no emulator), and they are held to the same **storage contract** as the Firestore adapters so they can't drift from Firestore's behavior.
- **Projections and replay records stay in memory even under `pnpm dev`**, because no Firestore adapter exists for them yet (the *store-to-port promotion* Later theme). The README says so.

**Depends on:** S7 (Firestore adapters — `done`)

**Scope files:** `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `firebase.json`, `firestore.indexes.json`, `functions/src/`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S9.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).
1. Write the storage contract (AC 1) and run it against the in-memory test doubles (AC 2). Where they differ from Firestore, change the doubles (store and return copies), not the contract. If a service turns out to rely on the old aliasing, that is a real production bug this story exists to find: fix it in `functions/src/`.
2. Run the same contract against the Firestore adapters behind the emulator guard (AC 3). Clear emulator state between cases with the emulator's `DELETE /emulator/v1/projects/<id>/databases/(default)/documents` endpoint on `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST`, and take the project ID from `GCLOUD_PROJECT` (which `firebase emulators:exec` sets) rather than a hard-coded one.
3. Split `local-server.ts` into a testable `createLocalServer` that takes its repositories, and an entrypoint that always uses Firestore (AC 4). Remove the `BT_USE_FIRESTORE` switch.
4. Add `firebase-tools`, the `dev` and `test:emulated` scripts, and the index file (AC 5–6); document local development (AC 7–8).
5. Set `status: done`, run `pnpm backlog:build`, update the Current baseline (the "Firestore" and "Emulator-based `pnpm dev`" rows), run `scripts/audit.sh story S9`, add the `CHANGELOG.md` entry, commit.

It seeds from the committed fixtures through `FixtureMlbStatsClient`: the file names `FixtureMlbStatsClient`, `2024-07-04`, and `744834`, so the real game with its plays is stored, not a toy object. It declares at least five `it(` cases, covering:

### S46 — Repository ports + shared storage contract + versioned snapshots

**Gap:** ADR-018: access only through repository ports — including the projection and replay stores — and one shared repository test suite run against every adapter; ADR-022: every update carries a monotonic `version`. At HEAD `GameProjectionRepository` (`functions/src/services/projection-store.ts`) and the replay-artifact repository (`replay-store.ts`) are declared in `functions/`, not `packages/ports`; the in-memory repositories hand back the stored object itself (the aliasing S9 found); and `GameSnapshot` / `ScheduleDay` carry `fetchedAt` but no `version` or `lastChangedAt`. Carries S9's contract cases (a)–(e) now that S9 is superseded. Inserted by the 2026-10-18 backlog review (two independent fresh-context reviewers, merged).

**Impact:** Before S46, the in-memory stores behaved differently from a real database, and nothing could tell a new game update from a stale one. S46 impact: every store is held to one shared set of behaviors, and every game and schedule carries a version so a late or repeated update can never overwrite a newer one.

**Source:** Pillar: Flexible — moving off a single-provider platform onto standard, swappable pieces behind ports (ADR-017–022). ### S54 — Budgets in pnpm verify: bundle size, render-count harness, coverage ratchet

**Gap:** ADR-026: at most 200 KB gzipped JavaScript before the page is usable, render-count baselines for heavy views, and coverage floors of 95% (domain) and 85% lines / 80% branches elsewhere. The owner chose to ratchet (2026-10-19): floors go to today's measured values now and every story raises them until the targets are met by the end of the UI band. Measured at HEAD by the reviewers: domain 94.5% lines / 79.5% branches, web 48.5% / 85%, functions 80% / 78%; floors are far lower (web lines 14). No `size-limit`. At `58db7c2` the web build is one entry chunk of 143,833 bytes gzipped (~140 KB), so the 200 KB budget holds with ~60 KB of headroom; `tools/` (S52's lint-rule tests) is not a workspace package and has no coverage floor, so AC 3's "every package" means `packages/*`, `functions` and `web`. **Re-measured at `1967ae3` (2026-10-20 backlog review):** lines / branches / functions / statements: domain 95.95 / 87.5 / 94.28 / 95.95 (already at the 95 target), mlb-api 100 / 88.05 / 100 / 100, functions 80.01 / 78.21 / 87.77 / 80.01, web 47.35 / 84 / 69.81 / 47.35; one entry chunk of 143,827 B gzipped. `packages/ports` is interfaces only: no runtime code, no tests and no coverage block (v8 reports 0% lines for its re-export `index.ts`), so AC 3's floors apply to the packages with runtime code and ports stays without one. **AC 1's 1 KB test cannot read `web/dist`:** `pnpm verify` runs `test:coverage` before `pnpm build`, so on a clean checkout (CI) there is no `dist` yet. The test runs `size-limit` on a temp file instead, under `tools/` like S53's `jscpd` test (picked up by `pnpm test:tools`), and `pnpm verify` runs `size-limit` after `pnpm build`; `tools/` was added to the fence for it. ### S59 — Web session: session provider, local dev sign-in, signed-out hides Settings

**Gap:** ADR-014 rule 7 puts session and entitlements in their own provider; ADR-027 makes Settings signed-in only (owner, 2026-10-19: "Hide settings for signed out users. Settings aren’t available without signin") and builds on the local dev sign-in now. S8 gives the server `GET /api/v1/me` with a `dev:` session; `web/` has no session concept, and the Settings route and nav item are always shown. Inserted by the 2026-10-19 design intake review (two independent fresh-context reviewers, merged).

**Impact:** Before S59, the web app had no idea who was using it, and Settings was open to everyone. S59 impact: the app knows when you are signed in, a developer can sign in locally with one click, and signed-out visitors no longer see Settings.

**Source:** Feature: Modern membership; Settings (favorites, hide scores, playback prefs)

**Design:** S34, S56 — build to the approved frames. This story may only move to `doing` once every design story named here is `done` (rule 18; `pnpm backlog:check` enforces it).

**Depends on:** **S8** (`/api/v1/me` and the `dev:` session).

**Scope files:** `web/src/`, `web/vitest.config.ts`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**API layer (2026-10-23 backlog review, after S49):** the web app calls the API only through the one `openapi-fetch` client in `web/src/api/client.ts` (`api.GET("/api/v1/me")`; S49). Three things follow for this story. (a) `/me` answers 401 when signed out, and the module's `unwrap` throws on any non-OK response. The session must read a 401 as "signed out" (check `response.status`), not as an error state. **Gap:** ADR-028 (owner, 2026-10-23): every place BT keeps personal data must be reachable by one deletion path, enforced in code where possible and by review where not. ### S77 — Account export and deletion API: download first, then delete everywhere, with maximal verification

**Gap:** ADR-028 (owner, 2026-10-23): a user downloads their data and only then deletes it (*"Yes, but only if download happens before delete"*); deletion is immediate, after maximal verification including a typed phrase (*"Immediately, but with maximal verification including typing a phrase"*); and backups are handled by a deletion log re-applied after any restore. After S76 every store is registered with `exportFor` / `deleteFor`, but no route calls them, nothing checks the confirmation, and nothing records a deletion. The session (S8) is a signed token checked without a database read, so a deleted user's session still verifies until it expires; routes must not treat that as an account.

**Impact:** Before S77, there was no way for a user's data to be downloaded or erased. S77 impact: the server can hand a signed-in user all of their data and then, once they've confirmed every way we can ask, erase it from every place it's kept, at once.

**Source:** Feature: Delete your data

**Depends on:** **S76** (the registry and stores), **S8** (session, `IdentityAdmin`), **S44** (route table).

**Scope files:** `packages/domain/`, `packages/ports/`, `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `openapi/`, `web/src/api/generated/`, `web/src/api/generated.types.test.ts`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S77.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S77.sh` performs)

1. `GET /api/v1/me/export`, signed in, returns every registered store's `exportFor(uid)` keyed by store name, plus a single-use deletion token bound to that uid that expires within 15 minutes; signed out it is 401 (test).
2. `POST /api/v1/me/delete` with the typed phrase and the deletion token deletes only when all hold, and each refusal is tested: the session was issued within the last 10 minutes (else 403, re-sign-in required); the phrase equals the one exported constant exactly (else 400); the token is valid, unused, unexpired, for this uid and came from an export (else 403, export required).
3. A successful delete runs `deleteFor` on every registered store and `IdentityAdmin.deleteAccount` for each linked identity, then `GET /api/v1/me` with the same session is 401 and no store holds anything for that uid (test). If a store fails, the request fails and a retry finishes the deletion (test with a store that fails once).
4. A deletion log records only the deleted uid and the time, and a `reapplyDeletions` function deletes a uid that a restored backup brought back (test). The deletion log is labeled in S76's classification manifest as the one entry ADR-028 keeps after a deletion (a `retained` label, which a test allows on that entry only); the single-use token record holds no personal field (token ID and expiry only) and is labeled too. (Added by the 2026-10-23 backlog review: S76's manifest fails on an unlabeled class, and `personal` would claim a store deletes the log.)
5. Both routes are in `ApiRoutes`, the spec and the web types (with their `generated.types.test.ts` pairings); `pnpm api:breaking` exits 0.
6. No `console.*` call in code this story adds logs an email or an export body (grep).
7. This file’s S77 **Status** (story heading and top table) is `done`.
